verdict.rationale: First-party MCP docs state that MCP gives ChatGPT or Codex access to third-party tools and context, such as browser or Figma tools. They walk through adding a concrete server (Context7), storing MCP configuration in `config.toml`, scoping servers per project, and reusing one configuration across clients. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP use, clear evidence of configuration in the ChatGPT chat/Work surfaces beyond Codex's config.toml, and details on transport and auth options.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects models to tools and context. Use it to give ChatGPT or Codex access to third-party documentation
to let it interact with developer tools like your browser or Figma
to add Context7 (a free MCP server for developer documentation)
you can also scope MCP servers to a project with `.codex/config.toml` (trusted projects only)
Once you configure your MCP servers, you can switch among those clients without redoing setup.
